To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hypoxic microenvironment in tumors reduces the production of MHC class I‐restricted antigenic peptides, and increases the expression of HLA/E and Qa‐l, and thereby reduces CD8+ T cell‐mediated immune response against tumor cells.
microenvironmental stress induces HLA‐E and Qa‐‐1 surface expression in tumor cells, and thereby reduces their recognition by CD8+ T lymphocytes.
hypoxia and glucose depletion in tumor cells induce HLA‐Qa‐1 surface presentation, which inhibits the CD8+ CTL response to the tumor‐associated antigen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how microenvironmental stresses affect the MHC class I‐mediated antigen presentation and CD8+ CTL responses, and may help to understand the mechanism of immune evasion of tumor cells.
the mechanism of how the microenvironmental stress modulates MHC class I expression, and provides a new insight into the mechanism of tumor escape from the immune system.
how the microenvironmental stresses affect the CD8+T‐cell response to tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia and glucose starvation can induce the stressed cells to escape from the immune surveillance through the modulation of MHC class I surface presentation.

hypoxia and/or glucose deprivation in the microenvironment of solid tumors can modulate both classical and nonclassical MICH class I presentation and thereby reduce CD4+ and CD8+ cytotoxic T‐cell responses.
microenvironmental stress induces HLA‐E and Qa‐I expression on the surface of stressed cells, and thereby reduces CD8+ T cell recognition of stressed cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microenvironmental stresses can modulate MHC class I surface expression, and thereby reduce CD4+ and CD8+ cytotoxic T‐cell recognition and responses to the stressed cells.
the tumor cells exposed to hypoxic and glucose deprived microenvironments could escape from the CD4+ T‐cell‐mediated immunity, but not CD8+ T cell‐mediated immunity.
hypoxic and nutrient‐deprived tumor cells can escape the CD8+T cell surveillance by reducing antigen presentation and inducing nonclassical MCH class I expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stressed tumor cells are able to escape from the immune system by modulating both the classical and the nonclassical MICH class I presentation.
hypoxia, glucose deprivation and other stresses that occur in solid tumors can modulate both classical and nonclassical MCH class I presentation and thereby affect the CD8+T‐cell response.
the tumor microenvironment can modulate the CD8+ response by affecting the expression of classical MHC I molecules as well as nonclassical MCH I molecules.
